prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 7.17. Exact Sanskrit: तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते ।
प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः ॥ १७ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Of these, the jñānī who is ever-united (nitya-yukta) and of single-pointed devotion (eka-bhakti) is distinguished. For I am exceedingly dear to the jñānī, and that one is exceedingly dear to Me. Chapter context: Knowing the divine, nature, qualities, devotion and the many manifestations. Paint the named element or manifestation in this verse; do not replace all with a deity portrait. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: O Bharatarṣabha Arjuna, four kinds of virtuous people (sukṛtinaḥ) worship Me: the distressed (ārta), the seeker of knowledge (jijñāsu), the seeker of wealth (arthārthī), and the wise (jñānī). Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: All of these are indeed noble; but the jñānī, I hold, is My very Self. For that one, with a unified mind (yuktātmā), abides in Me alone as the supreme goal (anuttamāṃ gatim). Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 7.17: Of these, the jñānī who is ever-united (nitya-yukta) and of single-pointed devotion (eka-bhakti) is distinguished. For I am exceedingly dear to the jñānī, and that one is exceedingly dear to Me.
